name: Chile
tagline: Desert, glaciers, volcanoes and vineyards stretched along the Pacific, with Easter Island far offshore.
cardDescription: A long, thin country from the Atacama Desert to Patagonia, with wine valleys, volcanoes, Easter Island and some of the best hiking on Earth.
metaDescription: A complete Chile travel guide: the 10 best places to visit, from Santiago and Valparaiso to the Atacama, Torres del Paine and Easter Island, with practical tips, a two-week itinerary and costs.

image.alt: The Cuernos del Paine peaks above a lake in Patagonia

intro: Chile is a ribbon of land about 4,300 kilometres long and rarely more than 180 wide, squeezed between the Andes and the Pacific. That shape gives it extreme variety: the driest desert on Earth in the north, Mediterranean vineyards in the middle, lakes and volcanoes in the south and glaciers and granite peaks in Patagonia.

Santiago is the capital and the usual starting point, a modern city beneath the Andes. From there, most visitors head north to the Atacama for stargazing and salt flats, or south to the Lake District and Patagonia for volcanoes, forests and the Torres del Paine trekking circuit. Easter Island, a Polynesian outpost 3,700 km offshore, is a destination of its own.

Chile is safe, well organised and easy to travel in, with excellent food and wine. The long distances mean flights are often the best option, so choose a few regions rather than trying to see everything. Seasons are reversed from the northern hemisphere, so plan for December to February as summer.

practicalIntro: The essentials, current for 2026. Chile is straightforward for most visitors, but check official sources before you travel.

practical.language: Spanish is the official language. English is spoken in tourism, but less so elsewhere.
practical.currency: Chilean peso (CLP). Roughly 900-1,000 pesos to the US dollar in recent years.
practical.money: Cards are widely accepted. Carry cash for rural areas, markets and small shops. ATMs are common.
practical.visa: Many nationalities, including the US, UK, EU and Australia, can enter visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days, but rules change, so check before you go.
practical.plugs: Type C and L, 220 V, 50 Hz. Bring an adaptor.
practical.emergency: 133 for police, 131 for ambulance, 132 for fire. 911 is not used.
practical.tipping: Around 10% is customary in restaurants and is often added to the bill as a suggested tip.
practical.safety: Chile is one of the safest countries in South America. Take normal precautions against pickpockets in cities, follow advice on volcanoes and trails, and be prepared for earthquakes.
practical.connectivity: Good in cities and towns, patchy in Patagonia and the Atacama. Local SIMs from Entel, Movistar or Claro are inexpensive.
practical.timeZone: Chile Standard Time (UTC-4), with daylight saving in the southern summer. Easter Island is two hours behind the mainland.

bestTime.headline: November-March
bestTime.summary: Southern summer, from November to March, is best for Patagonia, the Lake District and Chiloe.

seasons.text: Long days and open trails in the south.
Autumn colours, wine harvest and fewer crowds.
Spring, with the Atacama and Santiago at their best.
Ski season in the Andes, but cold and wet in the south.

bestTime.avoid: Winter in Patagonia, when trails, refugios and ferries close.

culture.intro: Chileans are polite, warm and a little formal, and family and conversation matter. Greeting and farewell customs are important, and punctuality is relaxed socially.

etiquette.title: Greet properly
etiquette.text: A handshake in business, a single cheek kiss in social settings.

etiquette.title: Be polite with titles
etiquette.text: Use senor and senora until invited.

etiquette.title: Respect nature
etiquette.text: Follow Leave No Trace in parks.

donts: Do not ignore volcano or weather alerts

tipsIntro: The things that most often catch visitors out in Chile.
tips: Book Torres del Paine refugios and Easter Island flights months ahead.
Flights are cheaper if booked early.
Carry layers, since weather changes quickly.
Check for ferry and road closures in Patagonia.
Watch for pickpockets in city centres.
Know earthquake procedures at your hotel.

faq.a: Yes, it is one of the safest countries in South America.

faq.q: How many days do I need?
faq.a: Ten to fourteen days for a good trip.
Many nationalities do not for stays up to 90 days, but check.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: November to March for Patagonia, and March to May or September to November for the north and centre.
It is moderately pricey, especially Patagonia and Easter Island.

faq.q: Can I see everything in one trip?
faq.a: No, choose two or three regions.
